title: openapi-proxy: filter, merge and convert OpenAPI documents on the edge
excerpt: An open source OpenAPI toolchain on the edge. Filter, merge and convert the OpenAPI documents your backends generate, and serve each result at a stable URL that stays current with your APIs. Set it up in a browser, or from a file in your repository.
content_html:
The OpenAPI toolchain
that lives on the edge.

Filter, merge and convert the OpenAPI documents your backends generate, and serve each result at a URL that stays current with your APIs. Your docs, your SDKs and your partners each get the part they need, without a line of code in your backends.

Or start in your repository: npx @pipe0/openapi-proxy init <url or file>

Open source. Free to start here, or deploy it to your own Cloudflare account. View on GitHub

One OpenAPI document. Many consumers.

Docs, SDKs, partners, tests and agents each need a different subset of your operations. Each subset becomes a variant, served at its own URL and current with the source.

Ship the endpoint now. Publish it when it is ready.

A new operation stays out of a variant until you include it. Publishing it is a click in the app, or a line in a file that is reviewed like the rest of your code.

Two ways to use it.

From a URL

Your OpenAPI document is at a URL. The service reads it, keeps reading it, and you choose in the app what each audience gets.

Connect a URL

From your repository

What each audience gets is written in a file next to your code. You serve it on localhost while you work, and deploy it from CI.

Read the guide

Both make the same project, at the same URLs. One that starts in the app can move into a repository later.

What people use it for

Public docs without internal endpoints

Check the tags and operations that are public. The variant serves those and exactly the schemas they reference, so no internal model is left behind in components.

Read the post

A document for each SDK and partner

Every selection gets its own URL, as JSON and YAML. Your docs read one, your SDK generator another, a partner a third. Who sees what is changed in the app, or in a file you review like code.

Read the post

Several services, one document

Merge the documents of up to ten services into one. Two schemas that share a name but not a meaning are told apart, and you are shown what the merge did.

Read the post

OpenAPI 3.0 for the tools that need it

Serve a variant as 3.0 or 3.1, whichever of the two your framework generates. Where 3.0 cannot say something, you are told exactly what was left out.

Read the post

Hear when your API changes

Each check compares operations, not text. You get an email that says what was added, changed or removed, and which variants it touches.

Read the post

Current by itself

The service keeps reading your document's URL, or takes the document your pipeline uploads with each deploy. A failing API never turns into an error for your readers: they get the last good copy.

Read the docs

In your repository, if you like

Keep what each audience gets in a file next to your code. One command serves your variants on localhost while you develop, another deploys them from CI.

Read the docs

Private sources stay private

A document behind authentication is fetched with headers you provide, stored encrypted and only ever sent to that document's own origin.

A workspace for the team

Invite your colleagues. Everyone works on the same projects and variants, so the public docs do not depend on one person being around.

A filter written by hand keeps more than it shows.

The usual shortcut is a loop in the backend that drops paths by tag. It rarely touches the schemas, so the public document still describes every internal request and response, for anyone who scrolls down.

Free to start.

Every feature is in both plans. Compare plans

Free$0

Enough for most teams: a few APIs, each with its audiences.

  • 3 projects
  • 15 variants
  • 5 MB per project

Pro$69 per year

For companies with many APIs, or many audiences for them.

  • 100 projects
  • 100 variants per project
  • 5 MB per project

On your own account

openapi-proxy is open source and runs on Cloudflare Workers. Deploy it to your own account and there is no plan to buy.

Read the source

Start with the document you already have.

Or keep it in a file next to your code and deploy it from CI. In your repository
